description: (SEE ATTACHMENT FOR PDF COPY OF THE LETTER BELOW) OFFICE OF INSPECTOR GENERAL U.S. ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY August 22, 2024 Dear EPA contractors: Consistent with our statutory duty under the Inspector General Act of 1978, as amended, to prevent and detect fraud, waste, and abuse relating to the programs and operations of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the EPA Office of Inspector General is contacting entities with EPA contracts to remind them of certain responsibilities. Specifically, as detailed below, as a contractor with the EPA, you must understand and adhere to statutory and regulatory requirements pertaining to reporting suspected fraud and other improper conduct and providing that information to your employees. The Federal Acquisition Regulation, or FAR, and the EPA Acquisition Regulation, or EPAAR, set forth requirements for EPA acquisitions and contractors. Accordingly, we remind you of the following FAR and EPAAR provisions: � Pursuant to 48 C.F.R. � 3.1002, all government contractors must conduct themselves with the highest degree of integrity and honesty. � Pursuant to 48 C.F.R. �� 3.1004 and 52.203-13, depending on the value and the length of the performance period of your contract, you may be subject to the Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct, which requires contractors to disclose to the OIG, in a timely manner and in writing, credible evidence of violations of federal criminal law involving fraud, conflict of interest, bribery, or gratuity violations, or a violation of the civil False Claims Act. These mandatory disclosures can be made through the EPA OIG website. � Pursuant to 48 C.F.R. � 3.1003, regardless of whether a contract with the EPA includes the Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct, a contractor may be suspended or debarred for knowingly failing to disclose to the government in a timely manner credible evidence of the statutory violations listed above. � Pursuant to 48 C.F.R. �� 1503.1004 and 1552.203-71, if the value of your EPA contract exceeds $1 million and you do not already have an established mechanism in place for your employees to report suspected improper conduct, you must prominently display the EPA OIG Hotline poster in all contractor facilities where contract work is performed. The Anti-Kickback Act of 1986 establishes that a person may not provide or accept, or attempt to provide or accept, a kickback. Pursuant to 48 C.F.R. �� 3.502-3 and 52.203-7, for contracts exceeding $150,000, a federal contractor must provide prompt notice, in writing, to the OIG or the U.S. attorney general if the contractor has reasonable grounds to believe that there has been a violation of the Anti-Kickback Act. In addition, whistleblower protections established by 41 U.S.C. � 4712 provide that an employee of a contractor may not be discharged, demoted, or otherwise discriminated against as reprisal for disclosing information to an OIG related to the contract that the employee reasonably believes is evidence of gross mismanagement or waste of federal funds; an abuse of authority or a violation or law, rule, or regulation; or a substantial and specific danger to public health or safety. We further remind you that, pursuant to 48 C.F.R. �� 3.906 and 52.203-17, contractors must inform their employees, in writing in the predominant language of the workforce or organization, of employee whistleblower rights and protections under 41 U.S.C. � 4712. The OIG has identified 2024 as its �Year of Fighting Fraud.� We encourage all contractors to report any suspected fraudulent or improper conduct relating to EPA contracts. You can reach us via the OIG Hotline or at OIG.Hotline@epa.gov or (888) 546-8740. The OIG will protect the confidentiality of complainants to the maximum extent permitted by law. Sincerely, Sean W. title: DSPO Connect Program for Suicide Prevention
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Personnel Readiness Management Agency (PRMA), formerly Defense Human Resources Activity (DHRA), Acquisition Management Directorate, intends to execute a non-competitive action in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(d) Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Government will negotiate and award a sole-source firm fixed price contract to SafeSide Prevention LLC, on behalf of the Defense Suicide Prevention Officer for the Connect Program for Suicide Prevention. The NAICS for this requirement is 541611 Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services, and the Product Service Code (PSC) is R425. The period of performance will include a base period and two, 12-month option periods beginning on or about September 4, 2026. The place of performance is at the vendor�s facility and various military installations. Description of Requirement The Defense Suicide Prevention Office (DSPO) requires a non-personal services Contractor to review, tailor, update, expand, and validate the Connect Program, previously known as the Wingman Guardian Connect Program, for the Department of War (DoW) and all Military Services (Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, National Guard Bureau, and Coast Guard). The Contractor shall validate the implementation of the Connect Program and provide a report that includes evaluation findings and recommendations for sustained program implementation and evaluation. The Connect Program (Wyman et al 2020; 2022) provides group interactive training for military personnel, followed by text messages and base-wide activities to embed concepts into culture and peer networks. The Connect Program�s interactive group design progresses from individual engagement (e.g., each participant shares career goals and values) to building group-level skills and norms (e.g., mapping group strengths). Specifically, participants learn together about and model skills to each other to grow and sustain �Four Cores� supportive of mental health and essential to job success: Kinship, Purpose, Guidance, and Balance. The vendor is required to have a sublicense for the Connect Program in order to tailor, update, and expand the Program. Justification for Noncompetitive Action The Connect Program is the only developed and tested community-based suicide prevention training program to achieve a Gold-Standard conducting randomized controlled trials with (1,500 Air Force) active U.S. military personnel that demonstrated significant reductions in suicide risk, depressive symptoms, and occupational problems where participants showed improved mental health outcomes. To achieve a Gold-Standard, a company must demonstrate a framework of rigorous, transparent, and ethical practices that ensure its findings are tested, valid, reproducible, and trustworthy. The Connect Program is the only community-based suicide prevention program with this level of evidence. It has taken several years for the Connect Program to conduct the trials and obtain the adoption needed for the Gold Standard. SafeSide Prevention, LLC is uniquely qualified as the only company that is sublicensed by Connect Media LLC to deliver and scale the Connect Program with fidelity and has a proven ability to adapt the program to new military and civilian markets. According to the market research, no other entity is granted sublicensing rights to the Connect Program nor will Connect Media LLC be issuing other sublicenses. Therefore, no other vendors can fulfill this requirement. As part of the market research, the Government communicated with the University of Rochester and Connect Media LLC, who holds perpetual, worldwide Copyright License, and were notified in writing by Connect Media LLC that no other vendors will be granted sublicensing rights to the Connect Program. The University of Rochester and Connect Media LLC provided the Government copies of their licenses, sublicense, and copyright agreements. Solicitation All responsible vendors that believe they can fully meet the Government's requirements may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. A vendor that believes it can meet the Government�s requirement must submit a copy of their sublicense agreement for the Connect Program, issued from Connect Media, LLC. Responses can be sent via e-mail to: Anne Ditch at anne.t.ditch.civ@mail.mil and Melissa Tamayo at melissa.s.tamayo.civ@mail.mil. title: ITS4US Deployment Accelerator Pilot
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice for the Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) for the project titled "ITS4US Deployment Accelerator Pilot". The Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Joint Program Office (JPO) looks to accelerate the replication of innovative technology solutions developed by large-scale deployment projects that it sponsors. ITS JPO believes that successful demonstration of these solutions by multiple agencies validates the technology's maturity and readiness for broader implementation across the industry. The purpose of this BAA is to award up to five (5) operational pilots that will test integrated technology solutions developed and deployed by the ITS4US Deployment Program. Each awardee will develop, test, and deploy solutions modeled on ITS4US deployment project documentation and its associated open-source software. In addition, the awardees will form a deployer cohort where they receive USDOT-funded technical support designed to accelerate implementation. Awardees can build faster, better, and cheaper by launching related efforts together, and use the insight of peers who have recently succeeded in addressing similar challenges.
